meta.title: Repot — move your dev environment to a new machine
meta.description: Repot scans your dev machine read-only and exports a readable restore script or native manifests. Secrets masked, no network, you review before you run.
meta.noscript: Repot moves your dev environment to a new machine.

tagline: Move your dev environment to a new machine — explained, selective, and safe.

hero.macHelp: Not sure which Mac? Apple menu › About This Mac lists a Chip on Apple silicon and a Processor on Intel.
hero.unknownHint: Repot is a desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux.
hero.betaNote: Builds are not code-signed or notarized yet, so your OS warns on first launch.
hero.screenshotAlt: Repot's review window: a sidebar of categories with item counts, a checklist of scanned items with descriptions, and a detail panel showing that three secrets in .zshrc will be masked.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Repot reads your development setup and turns it into a restore script or package lists for a new machine. Nothing on this machine is changed.

scan.title: Scan
scan.text: Repot reads package managers, runtimes, global packages, editor settings, and Git and shell configuration on this machine. Read-only.

select.title: Select
select.text: Review each item with its description and portability warnings, and keep only what you want. Pick the destination OS; items that cannot move there are disabled rather than guessed.

export.title: Export
export.text: Save a readable restore script or a bundle of native manifests. Copy the folder to the new machine, read it, and run it yourself.

how.screenshotAlt: Repot's export window previewing restore.sh: a file list on the left and the commented Bash script on the right.

principles.title: Built to be trusted with your machine

readonly.title: Never changes your machine
readonly.text: Scans are read-only, and Repot writes only to the export folder you choose. Whether to run the restore script is up to you.

secrets.title: Secrets masked
secrets.text: Detected secrets are replaced with <REDACTED> unless you allow the original value. Detection is pattern-based, so review exports before sharing.

network.title: No network
network.text: The app uses local data and built-in descriptions. The restore scripts you run separately can download packages through their respective tools.

review.title: Review before you run
review.text: Preview every file before saving, and read the exported script before executing it. It asks for confirmation, skips existing items and backs up configuration files.

tools.title: What Repot moves
tools.editor: VS Code and Cursor extensions, settings, keybindings and snippets
tools.git: User configuration and the configured global ignore file
tools.shell: zsh, Bash, fish and PowerShell profiles, oh-my-zsh custom plugins and themes, Starship configuration
tools.note: Package-manager entries can only move to the same OS (and Linux distribution family). Runtime managers are mapped between operating systems; unavailable items are disabled rather than guessed.

install.title: Install and first launch
install.lead: 0.x builds are unsigned betas: they are not code-signed or notarized, and there are no automatic updates yet, so your OS warns on first launch. Continue only after verifying that you trust the download.

mac: Open the .dmg and drag Repot to Applications.
Open Repot once. macOS says it cannot verify the developer.
Open System Settings › Privacy & Security, choose Open Anyway next to the Repot message, and confirm. This is needed only the first time.
windows: If SmartScreen blocks it, choose More info › Run anyway only if you trust the file.
linux: Make the AppImage executable, then open it:
Or install the .deb or .rpm with your distribution's package installer.
